subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Red Giants: A Star's Old Age
description: A micro-lesson that makes Red Giants: A Star's Old Age usable.

hook.text: When a star runs out of hydrogen in its core, it swells into a red giant—hundreds of times its original size.

buildup.text: The core contracts and heats up while the outer layers expand and cool, turning the star orange-red.

discovery.text: Helium fusion ignites in the core, producing carbon and oxygen. A second life begins inside a dying star.

twist.text: Arcturus, the bright orange star in Boötes, is a red giant. Our Sun will look like it in 5 billion years.

climax.text: Red giants shed their outer layers, enriching space with elements that form new stars and planets.

punchline.text: Stars don't just die. They swell, shed, and seed the next generation.

quiz.question: What causes a star to become a red giant?
options: It runs out of hydrogen fuel in its core, causing the outer layers to expand
A nearby star's gravity pulls its outer layers outward
It absorbs too much interstellar gas and swells

details.summary: When a Sun-like star exhausts its core hydrogen, the core contracts and heats up while the outer layers expand enormously, cooling and reddening — becoming a red giant. Our Sun will become a red giant in about 5 billion years, swelling to engulf Mercury, Venus, and possibly Earth.
details.whyItMatters: Red giants represent the future of our Sun and solar system. Understanding this transition reveals Earth's ultimate fate and explains the beautiful planetary nebulae created when these stars shed their outer layers.
takeaways: Stars become red giants when core hydrogen is exhausted
They swell enormously while their surfaces cool and redden
Our Sun will become a red giant in about 5 billion years

faq.question: How large do red giants become?
faq.answer: A Sun-like red giant can expand to 100-200 times the Sun's current radius, reaching Earth's orbit or beyond. The largest red supergiants like Betelgeuse are over 1,000 times the Sun's radius — if placed at the Sun's position, they would extend past Jupiter's orbit.

faq.question: What fuels a red giant if hydrogen is exhausted?
faq.answer: The core begins fusing helium into carbon and oxygen. Meanwhile, hydrogen continues fusing in a shell around the core. For more massive stars, successive fusion shells burn heavier elements. Each new fuel lasts shorter than the previous one.
